title: Tenses: Choosing and Using the Right Verb Form
summary: The main English tenses, past simple and past progressive in stories, present perfect or past simple, irregular verbs and how to keep your tense the same all the way through.

blocks.text: 1. What is a tense?

A **tense** is the form of a verb that shows **when** something happens: in the **past**, the **present** or the **future**. Choosing the right tense, and keeping it the same, is one of the easiest ways to make your writing clear and correct.

blocks.title: Words you need to know
items: **Base form**: the verb with nothing added: *go, eat, play*.
**Past participle** (3rd form): *gone, eaten, played*. Used after *have/has/had* and in the passive.
**Auxiliary (helping) verb**: *be, have, do, will, can...* used with the main verb.
**Progressive** (also called continuous): a form with *be + -ing* (*is running, was running*).
**Perfect**: a form with *have/has/had + past participle* (*has finished, had finished*).

blocks.text: 2. The main tenses

rows: She is walking to school now.
now, at the moment, today, this week
finished actions at a known past time
She was walking to school when it started to rain.
an action in progress in the past, often interrupted by a shorter action
while, when, at 8 o'clock last night
She has walked to school every day this term.
past actions connected to now / experiences / recent actions / unfinished time
ever, never, just, already, yet, since, for
She had already left when I phoned.
an action that happened **before** another past action
will + base form / am/is/are going to + base form
She will walk. / She is going to walk.
She has been walking for an hour.
an action that started in the past and is still going on

blocks.title: Questions and negatives
items: Present simple: *Do you **like** maths? / He **doesn't like** maths.* (after *do/does*, use the base form)
Past simple: *Did you **see** the match? / I **didn't see** it.* (after *did*, use the base form, not the past form)
Present perfect: *Have you **finished**? / I **haven't finished** yet.*

blocks.text: 3. Past simple and past progressive together

In stories (Paper 2) you will use these two tenses all the time. The **past progressive** sets the scene or shows a longer action; the **past simple** shows the short action that happens in the middle of it.

items: *I **was reading** in bed when the lights **went** out.* (long action + short interrupting action)
*While we **were eating** dinner, the phone **rang**.*
*The sun **was shining** and the birds **were singing**.* (setting the scene)

blocks.title: While or when?
blocks.text: Use **while** before the long action (past progressive) and **when** before the short action (past simple): *While I was walking, I saw a fox.* / *I was walking when I saw a fox.*
4. Present perfect or past simple?

rows: No finished time: *I **have visited** Luxor.* (at some time in my life)
Finished time is given: *I **visited** Luxor **last summer**.*
Result now: *I **have lost** my key.* (I still can't find it)
Just the past event: *I **lost** my key yesterday, but I found it.*
Unfinished time: *We **have lived** here **since** 2019 / **for** five years.*
Finished time: *We **lived** in Giza **for** five years.* (we don't now)

blocks.title: Since or for?
blocks.text: Use **since** with a starting point (*since Monday, since 2020, since I was six*). Use **for** with a length of time (*for two days, for a long time, for ten minutes*).

blocks.title: Never mix them
blocks.text: Do not use the present perfect with a finished time word: *I have seen him yesterday* ✗ → *I saw him yesterday* ✓
5. The past perfect: the earlier past

When you are already writing in the past and you need to go **further back**, use **had + past participle**. It helps the reader understand the order of events, especially in stories with a flashback.

items: *When we reached the station, the train **had** already **left**.* (the train left first)
*Sami was nervous because he **had** never **flown** before.*
*By the time the firefighters arrived, the neighbours **had put** out the fire.*

blocks.text: 6. Spelling the -ed and -ing forms

rows: stop → stopped, stopping / plan → planned, planning
change y to i before -ed; keep y before -ing
carry → carried, carrying / try → tried, trying

blocks.text: 7. Irregular verbs you must spell correctly
Irregular verbs do not take **-ed**. You have to learn them. These are the ones Year 6 students use (and misspell) most often.

blocks.title: Brought or bought?
blocks.text: **brought** comes from *bring* (carry something with you). **bought** comes from *buy* (pay for something). *I **bought** a cake and **brought** it to school.*
8. Keep your tense consistent
Choose one main tense for your writing and **stay in it**. Changing tense by mistake is one of the most common errors in Year 6 writing.

rows: Stories, recounts, diaries, biographies, news reports
**Past** (past simple + past progressive; past perfect for earlier events)
Information texts (non-chronological reports), reviews, persuasive texts
Plans, predictions, promises in letters and leaflets
**Future** (*will / going to*) where you talk about what is coming
*We arrived at the beach and Dad sets up the umbrella.*
*We arrived at the beach and Dad set up the umbrella.*
*Suddenly the door opens and a man walked in.*
*Suddenly the door opened and a man walked in.*

blocks.title: Changing tense on purpose is fine
blocks.text: Speech inside a story can be in any tense: *“I **am** so hungry,” Laila **said**.* The speech is present, the story is past. A news report can also end with the future: *The bridge **will reopen** next month.*
9. Common mistakes

blocks.title: Watch out for these
items: *He didn't went* ✗ → *He didn't **go*** ✓ (base form after *did*)
*Did you saw it?* ✗ → *Did you **see** it?* ✓
*I was go to school* ✗ → *I **went** / I **was going*** ✓
*She don't like it* ✗ → *She **doesn't** like it* ✓
*I have seen him yesterday* ✗ → *I **saw** him yesterday* ✓
*I have lived here since five years* ✗ → *I have lived here **for** five years* ✓
*He has went* ✗ → *He **has gone*** ✓ (past participle after *has*)

blocks.text: 10. How Checkpoint asks about it

**In the reading section**, a question can point to a verb in the text and ask you to name its **verb form**, or ask you to find a verb in a certain form. You may also be asked **why** the writer chose a tense.

blocks.title: Reading questions in this style
items: *Tick one box to show the verb form of the highlighted verb.* (for example: past progressive / present perfect / past simple)
*Find and copy a verb in the past progressive from paragraph 2.*
*Why is the information text written in the present tense?* → Because it gives facts that are true now.
*Why does the writer use the past progressive at the start of the story?* → To set the scene and show what was already happening before the main event.

blocks.title: Worked example (tick-one style)
blocks.text: *Text: ...Nour **was climbing** the last few steps when she heard a strange noise.* Which verb form is the highlighted verb? **A** past simple **B** past progressive **C** present perfect **D** present progressive. **Answer: B**, because it is *was* + *-ing*.

**In the writing section**, tenses are marked in **Grammar and punctuation** (7 marks). The examiner wants a **consistent** main tense and a **range** of verb forms used correctly. A story that mixes the past simple, past progressive and past perfect correctly shows you are working at a high level.

items: Set the scene with the past progressive: *Rain was falling and the wind was howling.*
Show an earlier event with the past perfect: *Nobody had opened that door for years.*
In a letter or report, use the present perfect for recent news: *The school has started a new reading club.*

blocks.title: نصيحة سريعة
items: أول ما تبدأ تكتب، قرر: القصة دي ماضي ولا مضارع؟ وفضل عليه لحد الآخر.
بعد did و didn't و does و doesn't الفعل يرجع لأصله: didn't go مش didn't went.
لو فيه كلمة زي yesterday أو last week أو ago يبقى past simple، مش has/have.

blocks.text: 11. Practice

items.q: Complete: *While I ______ (walk) home, I ______ (find) a wallet.*
items.a: *While I **was walking** home, I **found** a wallet.* (past progressive + past simple)
*I **have never seen** snow.* (present perfect: life experience)

items.q: Correct the mistake: *We have gone to Alexandria last summer.*
items.a: *We **went** to Alexandria last summer.* (finished time → past simple)

items.q: Complete: *By the time we arrived, the film ______ (start).*
items.a: *the film **had started**.* (past perfect: it happened before we arrived)

items.q: Which tense? *They are planting trees in the park this week.*
Correct the mistake: *Did you brought your football?*
Choose *since* or *for*: *My grandparents have lived in Aswan ______ 1985.*
Write the past simple and past participle of *choose* and *throw*.
Find the tense mistake and correct it: *The crowd cheered as the runners cross the finish line.*
items.a: *cross* → ***crossed***. The sentence is in the past, so both verbs must be past.

items.q: Why might a story begin: *The wind was howling and the waves were crashing against the rocks*?
items.a: The past progressive sets the scene: it shows what was already happening, which builds atmosphere before the main event.
